items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was my Captain... It was a while. When I first went in, I was in special weapons... It was Bobby Troup who began putting pressure... So they transferred me finally to the band.

ctx.x: What kinds of things would happen?

For instance, we had some fellows that went into town, in Jacksonville, North Carolina, the first guys that got liberty. They would go in – they went into town, and the police said, “There are no black Marines.” They weren’t as charitable about it as I’m being here. “There just are no black Marines. What are you doing with that uniform on?” They would insult them or threaten them, and so forth. The guys would challenge them, and they’d end up locking them up and bring them back – the MPs would have to get them…

But the conditions were really rough. We had some fellows who went, for instance, to Ohio, and met the same thing. They were – we were all proud. We were in a Marine uniform. Go home, you have the uniform on, and they were challenged by Army MPs. “What the so-and-so are you doing with that Marine uniform on?” The guy would say, “I’m a Marine.” “Get a load of this.” They would harass the guy. Of course, some of the fellows rebelled against it. One guy from Ohio spent his whole – I think he had two weeks of…

items.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998
items.q: I was in a unit that was being trained for small weapons... Bobby Troup... said that you might as well add him to the band. And I was transferred after boot camp to the band

ctx.x: But you did get to play in the band?

I did eventually. I was in a unit that was being trained for small weapons, a unit. And Bobby Troup, who was a lieutenant at that time, he knew that I was a musician and he finally said that you might as well add him to the band. And I was transferred after boot camp to the band, and later on I became the assistant bandmaster of the band.
You had to play for marches and assemblies and all that kind of thing?
